requirement:
Each line's structural and identity hashes are the SHA-256 digest of its
whitespace-separated words, using the unambiguous encoding under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Whitespace within a line does
not affect its hash; word boundaries remain significant.

The root hash encodes the nonblank lines in source order, including their line
boundaries. Inserting blank lines preserves it. Reordering distinct nonblank
lines or joining them changes the root's structural encoding.
The scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.sources.plain-text.fingerprints` has no implementation edges and no review roots. Every clause specifies observable behavior only, so no structural obligation needs implementation evidence.

- "Each line's structural and identity hashes are the SHA-256 digest of its whitespace-separated words, using the unambiguous encoding under `requirements.references.structural_hash`": this fixes the digest value. Any implementation that yields the same SHA-256 digest of the same word encoding, whichever library or code path it uses, satisfies the clause. No named library, signature, type, or delegation interface is prescribed. The encoding itself is defined by the cited `requirements.references.structural_hash`.
- "Whitespace within a line does not affect its hash; word boundaries remain significant": this is an input/output property.
- "The root hash encodes the nonblank lines in source order, including their line boundaries. Inserting blank lines preserves it. Reordering distinct nonblank lines or joining them changes the root's structural encoding": these are properties of the output value. They do not dictate how the code is built.
- "The scheme identifies these rules and their version under `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`": this is a citation. The trait method `fingerprint_scheme` and the `OutlineContent` accessors are declared under that cited requirement, not here.

No clause prescribes a signature, type, field, algorithm choice, or delegation that could be violated while preserving the observable results. Tests can supply the behavioral evidence.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover every behavioral obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.plain-text.fingerprints`.

**Line hashes are the SHA-256 of the whitespace-separated words, for both structural and identity hashes.**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[hashes_include_grammar_kinds_nesting_and_sha256_digests]` asserts the exact SHA-256 value for the line "hello". The comment gives the encoding as a tagged, length-prefixed text token.
- The same test asserts that the line's identity hash equals its structural hash.
- It also asserts the standard empty-input SHA-256 vector for the root and for its identity hash.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[plain_line_fingerprints_use_sha256_words_without_losing_boundaries]` asserts the same "hello" digest through the public API.

**Whitespace within a line does not affect its hash, and word boundaries stay significant.**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[plain_text_line_hashes_ignore_whitespace_but_not_word_breaks]` checks leading, trailing, tab and multi-space variants. All of them equal the original hash and equal `hash::line("two words")`.
- The same test asserts that `twowords` and `two word` differ from `two words`.
- `plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes` checks that selectors ignore spacing but separate `two words` from `twowords`.
- `plain_line_fingerprints_use_sha256_words_without_losing_boundaries` repeats both checks.

**The root hash encodes the nonblank lines in source order, including their boundaries.**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors]` compares `"alpha\n\nbeta\nalpha\n"` with other sources.
- Moving, adding and removing blank lines, and changing whitespace, leave `structural_hash()` equal. The compared source `"\n alpha \n beta\nalpha\n"` has a leading blank line and no blank line in the middle.
- Reordering to `beta, alpha, alpha` changes `structural_hash()`.
- Joining to `"alpha beta\nalpha\n"` changes `structural_hash()`.
- In the reorder and join cases, `fingerprint()` stays equal. That is consistent with the requirement, because the line identities are unchanged.

**The scheme identifies these rules and their version.** `plain_line_fingerprints_use_sha256_words_without_losing_boundaries` asserts the scheme string `plain-text-structural-v1:own-v1`.

The cited `requirements.references.structural_hash` and `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme` are context and were not reassessed. Several of these tests are also marked against `requirements.references.structural_hash`.

I found no behavior the requirement states that the tests would let through.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Each line's structural and identity hashes are the SHA-256 digest of its
whitespace-separated words, using the unambiguous encoding under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Whitespace within a line does
not affect its hash; word boundaries remain significant.
The root hash encodes the nonblank lines in source order, including their line
boundaries. Inserting blank lines preserves it. Reordering distinct nonblank
lines or joining them changes the root's structural encoding.
The scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
